Name of the Surah

• It is called al-Dhariyat (The Scattering Winds), because it is distinguished by its opening with God's oath by the Dhariyat, which are the winds that scatter dust and other things.

From the Aims of the Surah

• Affirming the occurrence of the Resurrection (al-ba'th) and recompense (al-jaza'), refuting the claims of those who deny it and the Messenger ﷺ, and clarifying their confusion regarding the Hereafter. It also includes the warning to those who deny of punishment on the Day of Resurrection, contrasted with the promise to the believers of bliss, and mention of some of their attributes.

• Clarifying the fate of the tyrannical nations that denied God's messengers, whom God destroyed with various kinds of punishment and devastation; a warning to the polytheists that what befell those deniers may befall them; clarifying the resemblance between the polytheists of Makkah and the deniers of earlier nations in what they accused the messengers of; and consoling the Prophet ﷺ by commanding him to turn away from them.

• Proving the oneness of God Most High through what is observed and perceived of His power, may He be glorified, in building the heaven and spreading out the earth, and clarifying the wisdom behind the creation of mankind, which is that God, Mighty and Majestic, be worshipped alone.

[The Tafsir]

God Most High swears by the winds that stir up dust, then by the clouds that carry a great weight of water, then by the ships that run upon the seas with ease and facility, then by the angels who distribute God's command among His creation. Indeed, what you are promised, O people, of resurrection and reckoning is surely true and certain, and indeed the reckoning and recompense for deeds will surely take place.

"Cursed be the liars, those who conjecture without knowledge, who are heedless and persist in deep immersion in disbelief and misguidance."

Commentary of King Fahd Complex (al-Tafsir al-Muyassar) on surah 51, verse 10–11:

"Cursed be the liars, those who conjecture without knowledge, who are heedless and persist in deep immersion in disbelief and misguidance."
These liars ask with a question that expresses disbelief and denial: "When is the Day of Reckoning and Recompense?"
The Day of Recompense is the day when they will be tormented by being burned in the Fire, and it will be said to them: "Taste your punishment, which you used to seek to hasten in the world."

Commentary of King Fahd Complex (al-Tafsir al-Muyassar) on surah 51, verse 19:

In their wealth there was a due right, obligatory and recommended, for the needy: those who ask people, and those who do not ask them out of modesty.

This is a commentary on Surah 51 (adh-Dhariyat), verse 20 — the verse ﴿وَفِي الْأَرْضِ آيَاتٌ لِّلْمُوقِنِينَ﴾.

Translation of the commentary:

"And on the earth are signs and clear proofs of the power of its Creator, for those of certainty [in faith] that Allah alone is the true God, with no partner, and for those who affirm His Messenger (ﷺ) as true."

And in your own selves (there are signs of Allah's power and lessons that guide you to the oneness of your Creator, and that there is no god worthy of worship for you besides Him). Will you not then see? Have you neglected them, so that you do not perceive them and take heed from them?
And in the sky is your provision, and that which you are promised of good and evil, reward and punishment, and all else besides, is written and decreed.

Commentary of the King Fahd Complex (al-Tafsir al-Muyassar) on Surah 51, verse 23:

God Most High swore by His noble Self that what He has promised you is true, so do not doubt it, just as you do not doubt your speech.

Has there come to you, O Messenger, the story of the honored guests of Ibrahim (Abraham)? They were noble angels. When they entered upon him in his house, they greeted him, saying, "Peace." He returned their greeting, saying, "Peace be upon you. You are a people unknown to us."

Then he turned aside secretly to his family, and brought a fat calf, slaughtered it, roasted it over the fire, then placed it before them, and gently urged them to the meal, saying: "Will you not eat?" Commentary of King Fahd Complex (al-Tafsir al-Muyassar) on surah 51, verse 35:

So We brought out those who were in the town of the people of Lot who were believers.
Then We found in that town no house other than one house of Muslims, namely the house of Lut (peace be upon him).

And We left in it (the mentioned town) a sign of the punishment, remaining as a token of Allah's power and of His vengeance upon the disbelievers; and that is a lesson for those who fear the painful, agonizing punishment of Allah.

In the sending of Musa (Moses) to Fir'awn (Pharaoh) and his chiefs with clear signs and evident miracles, there is a sign for those who fear the painful punishment. But Fir'awn turned away, relying on his power and his followers, and said of Musa: "He is a sorcerer or a madman."

The heaven We built with power, and We are indeed its expanders. (Tafsir al-Muyassar commentary)

Note: The text above is a rendering of the Qur'anic verse itself and should be read alongside the commentary.
The earth: We made it a bed (firash) for creatures, for them to settle upon, so how excellent are the ones who spread it out, We.
And from every kind of existing thing We created two different types, so that you may remember the power of Allah and take heed.

Then flee, O people, from the punishment of God to His mercy, by believing in Him and in His Messenger, following His command, and acting in obedience to Him. Indeed, I am a clear warner to you. And when the Messenger of God (ﷺ) was faced with a grave matter, he would turn to prayer, and this is fleeing to God.

Commentary of the King Fahd Complex (al-Tafsir al-Muyassar) on Surah 51, verse 51:

﴿And do not make another deity along with Allah. Indeed, I am to you a clear warner from Him.﴾

Commentary of the King Fahd Complex (al-Tafsir al-Muyassar) on surah 51, verse 52:

Just as Quraysh denied their prophet Muhammad (ﷺ), and said, "He is a poet, or a sorcerer, or a madman," so the nations that denied their messengers before Quraysh did the same, and God sent down His vengeance upon them.

Did the former and the latter generations enjoin one another to deny the Messenger, when they all said the same thing? Rather, they are a people of tyranny, whose hearts and deeds resembled one another in disbelief and transgression. So their later ones said what their earlier ones had said.

Commentary of King Fahd Complex (al-Tafsir al-Muyassar) on surah 51, verse 54:

So turn away, O Messenger, from the polytheists until there comes to them the command of Allah. You are not to be blamed for anyone, for you have conveyed what you were sent with.

With your turning away from them, O Messenger, and your not heeding their discouragement, persist in calling to God and in admonishing those to whom you were sent; for reminder and admonition benefit the people of believing hearts, and in them is the establishment of proof against those who turn away.
And I did not create the jinn and humankind except for a sublime purpose: that they worship Me alone, without anyone other than Me.

In the Quranic verse: "I do not want any provision from them, nor do I want them to feed Me." Then, "I am the Provider, the Giver." So He, glory be to Him, has no need of creation; rather, they are the ones in need of Him in all their circumstances. He is their Creator and their Provider, and free of need from them.

Indeed, Allah alone is the Provider (al-Razzaq) of His creatures, the One who has taken on the responsibility for their sustenance, the Possessor of strength, the Firm (al-Matin). He cannot be overcome or defeated; all power and strength belong to Him.

For those who did wrong by denying the Messenger Muhammad (ﷺ), there is a share of Allah's punishment descending upon them, like the share of their counterparts who passed away before them. So let them not seek to hasten the punishment, for it will surely come to them without doubt.

Then woe and destruction to those who disbelieve in Allah and His Messenger, on the Day they are promised, which is the Day when the punishment descends upon them, and that is the Day of Resurrection.
